_**User**_

/speckit-constitution Establish principles for an AI-powered Support Ticket Management System:

1. Domain integrity: The ticket lifecycle (OPEN→IN_PROGRESS→RESOLVED→CLOSED; OPEN/IN_PROGRESS→CANCELLED) is enforced exclusively by the backend domain layer. Any other transition is rejected. Clients are never trusted.
2. Validation at the boundary: all input is validated server-side; errors use one consistent, machine-readable error format with field-level details.
3. Test-first for deterministic logic: every state transition (valid and invalid) has an integration test against a real database before the feature is considered done.
4. Grounded AI only: the assistant answers solely from retrieved ticket context, never from general model knowledge. Every answer cites the ticket IDs it used. When retrieval finds nothing relevant, it says so explicitly. Fabrication is a defect, not a quality issue.
5. Knowledge freshness: any ticket create/update/close must refresh its embeddings; a stale knowledge base is a defect.
6. Configuration over hardcoding: retrieval parameters (top-K, similarity threshold), model names, and endpoints are externalized configuration.
7. Bounded AI scope: single retrieve→generate flow. The assistant never takes actions (no ticket creation, notifications, or tool chaining).
8. Security: no secrets in the repository, ever.
9. Simplicity: no abstraction without a current requirement.
10. AI accountability: AI-generated code and answers are reviewed, not trusted; mistakes are recorded in docs/ai-mistakes.md.

Mandated constraints: Java 21, Spring Boot, Spring AI, H2, a vector store (Redis), REST, React for frontend.

- Principle V: refresh triggers include ticket create, field updates, comment additions, and every status transition including cancellation. The intent to refresh MUST be recorded atomically with the ticket change (same database transaction); embedding generation MUST NOT run inside that transaction. - Principle II: invalid state transitions MUST be distinguishable from malformed input by both status code and error code.
- Quality gates: remove "lint, type checks"; require successful compilation and full test suite pass.

Bump the version according to the Governance section.

I amended `.specify/memory/constitution.md` from 1.0.0 to **2.0.0**. It's a doc-only change, so I ran no tests or build.

**Why 2.0.0 (MAJOR):** Governance says MAJOR is for backward-incompatible principle redefinitions. Principle IV's core rule was redefined and the mandated stack changed (H2 and Redis dropped). The Ratified date stays 2026-11-19, and Last Amended is also 2026-11-19 because the first version was written today.

**What changed**
- **II. Validation at the Boundary:** invalid transitions and malformed input must now use different HTTP status codes and different error codes. Neither may be reused for the other.
- **III. Test-First:** integration tests must run against a real, containerized PostgreSQL. H2 and persistence mocks are explicitly banned.
- **IV. Grounded AI:**
  - The "MUST NOT use general model knowledge" clause is replaced: every factual claim must trace to retrieved tickets.
  - Cited IDs must be a subset of retrieved IDs, verified in code after generation.
  - When nothing meets the similarity threshold, the no-relevant-tickets response is returned without calling the LLM.
  - Required tests now include a citation-subset violation case and a "LLM not invoked" case.
- **V. Knowledge Freshness:**
  - Refresh triggers are creation, field updates, comment additions and every status transition including cancellation.
  - The refresh intent is recorded in the same transaction as the ticket change, and embedding generation stays outside it.
  - Failed refreshes are retried, and a full reindex capability must exist.
  - Required tests cover intent recorded per trigger, nothing recorded on rollback, and retry on failure.
- **Technology Constraints:** PostgreSQL holds both relational data and vectors (PGVector in the same instance). Schema and seed data come only from versioned migrations. Spring Boot, Spring AI and the build tool are pinned in the plan and must not drift.
- **Quality Gates:** the lint and type-check requirement is gone. Merge now requires successful compilation and a full passing test suite.

**Choices of mine to check**
- Principle II says the two cases must differ in status code and error code, but I didn't name specific codes, such as 400 versus 409. That's left for the spec or plan.
- Principle IV keeps "answers solely from retrieved ticket context", which fits the new traceability rule. Say so if you want that sentence dropped.
- The build tool isn't named anywhere. The plan has to choose and pin it.
- I added the "nothing recorded on rollback" test requirement to Principle V, which you didn't ask for.

The Sync Impact Report at the top of the file is temporary, so delete it before committing. I didn't change any templates. `/speckit-plan` will need to pin the three versions.

_**User**_

/speckit-specify Ticket lifecycle management for a support team.

Context: Support agents track customer issues as tickets. This feature covers creating, viewing, updating, commenting on, finding, and moving tickets through their lifecycle. An AI assistant that answers questions over ticket history is a separate feature, but it depends on this one: this feature must capture every piece of information the assistant will need, and must ensure the assistant's knowledge never silently goes stale.

User stories (priority order):
- P1: An agent creates a ticket and views its full details.
- P1: An agent moves a ticket through its lifecycle. Allowed: OPEN→IN_PROGRESS→RESOLVED→CLOSED, OPEN→CANCELLED, IN_PROGRESS→CANCELLED. Any other move is rejected, the ticket is unchanged, and the agent is told the current status and which moves are allowed. Status changes are a dedicated action, separate from editing ticket fields.
- P2: An agent edits a ticket's title, description, priority, and assignee.
- P2: An agent adds comments to a ticket.
- P3: An agent lists tickets, searches them by keyword, and filters them by status.

Information a ticket carries: a human-readable identifier (e.g., TKT-1001), title, description, priority, assignee, category, status, resolution notes, creation and last-updated times, and its comments (each with author, text, and time). Category and resolution notes exist because the assistant needs them.

Rules:
- All input is validated; errors identify which fields are wrong and why.
- A malformed request and a not-allowed lifecycle move must be distinguishable from each other.
- Data survives a system restart.
- Every change to a ticket's content, status, or comments must be reflected in the assistant's knowledge. No such change may be lost, even if refreshing the assistant's knowledge temporarily fails.

Out of scope: the assistant itself, the user interface, authentication and roles, deleting tickets, attachments, notifications.

2. **Category:** a fixed list of Billing, Technical, Account, or Other. Anything else is refused as invalid input.
3. **Editing after CLOSED or CANCELLED:** comments can still be added. Title, description, priority, assignee, category, and resolution notes are frozen.
4. **Cancellation reason:** required and non-empty for the move to CANCELLED. It is saved on the ticket and cannot be changed afterwards.
5. **Identifier search:** an exact match on the identifier counts (typing TKT-1001 returns that ticket). A partial match such as 1001 does not.

**Spec updated:** `specs/001-ticket-lifecycle/spec.md`

- **Clarifications:** new section with a session entry for each of the five answers.
- **User stories:** knowledge and refresh scenarios in stories 1–4 reworded to the intent-only rule. New scenarios for frozen fields and comments on closed tickets (story 3, story 4), cancellation without a reason (story 2), and identifier search (story 5).
- **Edge cases:** knowledge-update cases reworded. New cases for a missing category, a missing cancellation reason, and frozen tickets.
- **Functional requirements:** FR-001, FR-003, FR-004, FR-010, FR-011, FR-012, FR-014 and FR-016 updated. FR-017 now says retry, visibility and rebuild belong to the assistant feature. FR-018 is marked as removed.
- **Key entities:** "Refresh intent" replaces "Knowledge update". Ticket gains the cancellation reason.
- **Success criteria:** SC-003, SC-005 and SC-006 updated to the intent-only outcomes.

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

Saved for later sessions in this project. This is the state of the work as of 2026-11-19.

## What we are building

Support agents track customer issues as tickets. The first feature, `specs/001-ticket-lifecycle`, covers creating, viewing, editing, commenting, finding, and moving tickets. An assistant that answers from ticket history is a later feature. This one only has to keep the information that assistant will need, and record that its knowledge must be refreshed.

## Design that is already fixed

Constitution v2.0.0 sets the stack and the rules.

- Java 21, Spring Boot, Spring AI, PostgreSQL with PGVector in the same database, REST, and React.
- Schema and seed data come only from versioned migrations.
- Spring Boot, Spring AI, and the build tool versions get pinned in the plan. They are not chosen yet.
- Only these status moves exist, and only the backend domain layer enforces them: OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED, and OPEN or IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED. Anything else is rejected and the ticket stays as it was.
- Every input is checked on the server. One error format, with the field and the reason. A badly formed request and a disallowed move must differ in both status code and error code. The actual codes are not chosen.
- Every transition, allowed and refused, gets an integration test against real containerized PostgreSQL.
- The refresh intent is written in the same database transaction as the ticket change. Generating the embedding happens outside that transaction.
- The assistant, when it exists, answers only from retrieved tickets, cites only ticket IDs it actually retrieved, and does not call the model when nothing is similar enough. It never creates tickets or calls tools.
- Top-K, the similarity threshold, model names, and endpoints are configuration.
- No secrets in the repository. No extra abstraction without a current need. The project must compile and the full test suite must pass.

## Decisions you confirmed today

1. This feature is done when the refresh intent is saved with the change, still there after a restart, and absent if the change rolls back. Retry, showing failures, rebuilding knowledge, and proving the knowledge matches move to the assistant feature. The constitution's freshness rule is not met for the whole system until that feature exists.
2. Category is Billing, Technical, Account, or Other. Anything else is rejected.
3. On a CLOSED or CANCELLED ticket, the fields are frozen. Comments can still be added.
4. Cancelling requires a written reason. It is saved and cannot be changed later.
5. Searching for TKT-1001 finds that ticket. Searching for 1001 does not match the identifier.

## Requirements for the first feature

- P1: create a ticket and view everything on it. P1: move it through the lifecycle. P2: edit title, description, priority, assignee, category, and resolution notes. P2: add comments. P3: list, search, and filter by status.
- A ticket has an identifier like TKT-1001, title, description, priority, an optional assignee, category, status, resolution notes, a cancellation reason once cancelled, created and updated times, and comments with author, text, and time.
- Changing status is its own action, separate from editing fields. A refused move tells the agent the current status and which moves are allowed.
- A badly formed request, a disallowed move, and a missing ticket are three different errors.
- Out of scope: the assistant, the screens, login and roles, deleting tickets, changing or deleting comments, attachments, and notifications.

## Still assumptions, not confirmed by you

Priority is Low, Medium, High, or Urgent. The assignee and the comment author are typed names, not accounts. New tickets start as OPEN. Identifiers start at TKT-1001. Resolution notes are required to resolve, can be corrected before close, and cannot be wiped. Lists show 20 at a time, newest update first. When two edits hit the same field, the later one wins.

Next step is `/speckit-plan`, which has to pin the three versions.

# Carry-over to 002-ticket-assistant

Purpose: items deferred from 001 or discovered early that the 002 spec/plan MUST address.
Consume when running /speckit-specify for 002; mark each item with where it landed.

## A. Moved out of 001 (MUST be specified in 002)
Source: 001 clarification session 2026-11-19, Q1; constitution Principle V

- [ ] A1. Process refresh intents: build the ticket's knowledge document, embed it, store it, mark the intent done.
- [ ] A2. Retry failed refreshes with backoff and a maximum attempt count; after that, mark them failed (no infinite retry).
- [ ] A3. Failure visibility: define WHO can see outstanding/failed refreshes and HOW (e.g., a count/list an operator can query).
- [ ] A4. Full rebuild of all embeddings from stored tickets and comments.
- [ ] A5. Verification that stored knowledge matches the current ticket (the removed "knowledge matches" acceptance scenarios).
- [ ] A6. Until 002 ships, the system does not meet Principle V. 002 is what closes that gap.

## B. Constraints already decided
- B1. The processor reads the ticket's CURRENT state when it runs, not a snapshot from when the intent was created; otherwise an older refresh can overwrite newer knowledge. Multiple pending intents for one ticket collapse into one refresh. (Source: 001 spec review, concurrency discussion)
- B2. Refresh triggers already recorded by 001: create, field edit, comment (including on CLOSED/CANCELLED tickets), every status move including cancel. (Source: 001 FR-016)
- B3. Knowledge-document source fields available from 001: identifier, title, description, priority, category (Billing/Technical/Account/Shipping/Other), status, assignee, resolution notes, cancellation reason, comments. (Source: 001 spec)
- B4. Vector table is created by a versioned migration; Spring AI's PGVector auto schema initialization MUST be disabled. (Source: constitution, Technology Constraints)
- B5. No relevant result above the threshold → return the "no relevant tickets" response WITHOUT calling the LLM. (Source: constitution Principle IV)
- B6. Top-K and similarity threshold are configuration, not code. (Source: constitution Principle VI)
- B7. Single retrieve → generate flow; no tool calling, no chained model calls. (Source: constitution Principle VII)

## C. Open questions 002 must answer
- [ ] C1. A cited ticket ID is not in the retrieved set: strip the citation, regenerate, or return the fallback answer? (Constitution IV says only "not returned as-is")
- [ ] C2. Document shape and chunking: one document per ticket, or separate chunks for description / comments / resolution? Paragraph vs fixed-size vs semantic splitting, justified for ticket data. (Assessment requires this documented in architecture.md)
- [ ] C3. Embedding model: local (Ollama) vs cloud; cost/latency/quality tradeoff. Note that the vector dimension is fixed in the migration, so changing models means a migration plus a full rebuild. Reviewers must be able to run it without your private credentials.
- [ ] C4. Questions like "Which high-priority tickets are related to payment?" need metadata filtering. Principle VII forbids a second LLM call to extract filters from the question, so how? Semantic search only, rule-based filter detection, or explicit filter parameters on /api/ai/ask?
- [ ] C5. Should CANCELLED tickets be retrievable? Should "similar resolved tickets" filter on status?
- [ ] C6. Does Spring AI's PgVectorStore join the Spring-managed transaction or use its own connection? Verify against the pinned version; don't assume. (Source: instructor's unverified claim, see ai-mistakes M-006)

_**User**_

/speckit-plan Technical plan for 001-ticket-lifecycle.

Versions (pinned; do not change):
- Java 21
- Spring Boot 4.1.2   (Spring AI 2.0.x supports Boot 4.0/4.1 only)
- Spring AI 2.0.2: pinned for later features; NOT a dependency of this feature
- Build: Maven 3.9.12 with wrapper

Architecture:
- Single Spring Boot service, layered: web (controllers, DTOs) → application (use cases, transactions) → domain (Ticket aggregate with the state machine) → persistence.
- State machine lives only in the domain model (constitution I).
- PostgreSQL with the pgvector image via docker-compose for local runs; Flyway for schema and seed data; seed data dev-only.
- Ticket identifier from a database sequence starting at 1001, formatted TKT-<n>.
- Refresh intent: an outbox table written in the same transaction as every ticket change; no processing in this feature.
- Concurrency: pessimistic row lock on the ticket for every status move and edit, so a losing request is re-evaluated against committed state (spec Story 2 scenario 10).
- Search: case-insensitive substring across the spec's fields plus an exact-identifier match; no full-text engine (constitution IX).
- Pagination: 20 per page, ordered by last-updated desc.

API:
- Field edits via one endpoint; status changes via a separate transitions endpoint.
- Errors: RFC 9457 problem details with a stable errorCode. 400 for malformed input and field validation; 409 for disallowed transitions (include currentStatus and allowedTransitions); 404 for unknown tickets.
- Unknown fields in request bodies are rejected.

Testing:
- Integration tests with Testcontainers PostgreSQL (no H2, no persistence mocks).
- Full transition matrix (every from/to pair), concurrency tests for both races, and outbox tests (intent on commit, none on rollback).
- Deterministic transition tests written first.

---

The plan for `001-ticket-lifecycle` is written, with research, data model, API contract and quickstart. Nothing has been built or run. The plan clears the Constitution Check with one exception: Principle V is only partly met.

I checked the pins before writing. Spring Boot 4.1.2, Spring AI 2.0.2 and Maven 3.9.12 all exist on Maven Central, and `pgvector/pgvector:0.8.7-pg17` exists on Docker Hub. Spring AI is recorded as pinned but is not a dependency of this feature.

## Two things to know first

1. **Principle V is only partly met.** This feature records and tests the refresh intent. Retry, failure visibility and full reindex are in 002, as you decided in the clarifications. The constitution says a feature isn't done until retry is tested, so I put this in the plan's complexity table. Either don't release 001 before 002 lands, or get explicit reviewer sign-off in the PR.
2. **No JDK 21 on this machine.** Only JDK 25 is installed. The plan adds a build check that requires Java 21 and Maven 3.9.12, so the first build will fail until you install JDK 21. The check is a Maven plugin you didn't ask for, which I added to enforce "must not drift".

## Decisions I made where your brief was silent

Please confirm or overrule these. Each is a small change to reverse.

| # | Decision |
|---|----------|
| D1 | Editing a closed or cancelled ticket returns 409 `TICKET_FROZEN`. Setting resolution notes on a ticket that has none returns 409 `RESOLUTION_NOTES_NOT_EDITABLE`. Your brief only covered transitions for 409. |
| D2 | Check order is validation (400), then ticket lookup (404), then ticket state (409). |
| D3 | The edit endpoint is a `PATCH`. A missing or null field means unchanged. A blank `assignee` clears it, which the spec doesn't mention. An empty body is a 400. |
| D4 | A field that doesn't belong to the target status is a 400. For example, `resolutionNotes` on a move to `IN_PROGRESS`. |
| D5 | Adding a comment also takes the row lock. A comment updates the ticket's last-updated time, so without the lock it could overwrite a concurrent change. |
| D6 | The API uses the spec's spelling for priority and category (`Low`, `Billing`). The database stores `LOW`, `BILLING`. |
| D7 | Cancellation reason is not searchable. The spec's list of searchable fields leaves it out. |
| D8 | The search keyword is trimmed and `%`, `_` and `\` match literally. An identifier match needs the exact form `TKT-<n>`, so `TKT-01001` doesn't match. |
| D9 | The dev seed data also writes a refresh intent for each seeded ticket, so the assistant doesn't start out stale. |
| D10 | Package `com.example.tickets` and the `backend/` folder are placeholders. |
| D11 | A 5-second Postgres lock timeout, returning 503 `TICKET_BUSY`, so a stuck lock can't hang a request. |

## Unconfirmed items

Two things I couldn't check, so the first implementation task has to:
- The exact setting that rejects unknown JSON fields under Jackson 3. If the Spring Boot 3 property name doesn't work, the fallback is an annotation on each request class.
- The Boot 4 MockMvc test class names.

## Behaviors the plan guarantees

- **Validation reports every bad field.** Request fields are checked as strings first, so a bad priority and a blank title come back together, as SC-003 requires.
- **Concurrency tests don't depend on timing.** They repeat both races many times. A deterministic variant holds the row lock itself, queues the request, commits a competing change, and checks the queued request saw it.
- **Rollback is tested on the real database.** Temporary database triggers force a failure, once on the intent write and once at commit.

**Refining ticket lifecycle logic**

I'm integrating a new edge case into the ticket lifecycle specifications. My focus is on how to handle tickets held up by other ongoing changes for an extended period. The requirement is to refuse these requests, marking them as temporarily unavailable after a defined wait time. This aims to prevent indefinite holds and improve system responsiveness.

**Adding hold retry logic**

I've introduced a fourth distinct outcome for ticket progression: a guided "retry later" scenario. This occurs when a ticket remains unchanged, and no refresh intent is logged, effectively being distinct from malformed input, disallowed moves, or missing tickets. I've ensured only this specific edge case is added, meticulously noting the precise lines modified.

**Documenting ticket status exceptions**

I'm detailing scenarios where ticket moves are problematic. This includes moves to already closed or cancelled states, which are now clearly categorized as malformed input. Additionally, I'm defining responses for attempts to move tickets to their current status, or when required fields like resolution notes or cancellation reasons are missing.

**Considering ticket state conflicts**

I'm exploring scenarios where concurrent requests might conflict with ticket states. Specifically, I'm looking at how edits to saved resolution notes are refused and how refresh intent recording fails due to a shared save operation. The system's behavior on restart is also being clarified, ensuring changes and intents persist.

**Clarifying ticket state conflicts**

I'm refining how concurrent requests are handled by ensuring every move and edit is evaluated against the ticket's state at save. This prevents disallowed moves and edits to frozen tickets, with the loser of a race condition being evaluated against the updated state. Last-write-wins now specifically applies to concurrent edits of editable tickets.

**Handling state changes**

I'm now detailing edge cases where a search keyword matches nothing, or a status filter yields no results, resulting in an empty agent list. I'm also refining how tickets held too long by other changes are refused with a "retry later" message, distinct from other negative outcomes.

**Adding new edge case logic**

I'm implementing a new scenario where tickets held too long by other processes will be marked as temporarily unavailable, with instructions to retry. This is a distinct outcome from other error types, and it ensures the ticket state remains unchanged without recording any refresh intent.

_**User**_

## M-007 · Instructor predicted the wrong constitution version bump
- **Date / Phase:** 2026-11-19 · Constitution amendment
- **Tool:** Claude (chat instructor)
- **Category:** UNGROUNDED-ANSWER
- **AI said:** The amendment should produce v1.1.0 (MINOR).
- **Actually true:** The amendment redefined Principle IV and swapped the mandated stack; under the constitution's own Governance rules that is MAJOR → v2.0.0. The spec-kit command applied the rules correctly and explained why.
- **How caught:** Compared the generated Sync Impact Report against the Governance versioning rules.
- **Fix:** Accepted 2.0.0.
- **Prevention:** Re-apply the rules after the scope of a change changes; don't reuse an earlier prediction.

## M-008 · Category list did not cover the requirements' own examples
- **Date / Phase:** 2026-11-19 · /speckit-specify, /speckit-clarify (001)
- **Tool:** Cursor (spec-kit)
- **Category:** INVENTED-REQUIREMENT
- **AI said:** First, category as free text ("words the assistant can use"); then, in clarify, a fixed list of Billing, Technical, Account, Other.
- **Actually true:** Category is a RAG metadata filter, so free text fragments it ("Payment" vs "payments"); and the requirements example "common causes of shipment tracking issues" has no matching category, so it would fall into Other.
- **How caught:** Checked the category values against the requirements document's example questions.
- **Fix:** Fixed list Billing, Technical, Account, Shipping, Other (post-clarify amendment).
- **Prevention:** Check every enumerated value against the source requirements and example queries.

## M-009 · Untestable success criterion for a backend-only feature
- **Date / Phase:** 2026-11-19 · /speckit-specify (001)
- **Tool:** Cursor (spec-kit)
- **Category:** INVENTED-REQUIREMENT
- **AI said:** SC-001 "An agent can create a ticket and open its full details in under one minute."
- **Actually true:** The feature has no UI; a human timing target is not measurable by an automated test and measures nothing about the system.
- **How caught:** Manual spec review against the "every criterion must be testable" rule.
- **Fix:** SC-001 deleted.
- **Prevention:** Success criteria must be checkable for the feature's actual scope.

## M-010 · Last-write-wins would break the non-negotiable state machine
- **Date / Phase:** 2026-11-19 · /speckit-specify, /speckit-clarify (001)
- **Tool:** Cursor (spec-kit)
- **Category:** WRONG-CODE (design defect)
- **AI said:** "Two agents change the same ticket … the last accepted change is stored; no conflict detection."
- **Actually true:** Two concurrent moves from OPEN (→IN_PROGRESS and →CANCELLED) would both validate against OPEN; the later write could turn a CANCELLED ticket into IN_PROGRESS, a forbidden transition (Constitution I, NON-NEGOTIABLE). The same race allows edits on frozen tickets.
- **How caught:** Manual review combining the concurrency assumption with the state machine; neither specify nor clarify flagged it.
- **Fix:** Spec requires every move/edit to be evaluated against the state at save time; plan uses a pessimistic row lock; concurrency tests for both races.
- **Prevention:** For any concurrency rule, check it against every invariant in the constitution.

## M-011 · Plan claimed create takes a row lock
- **Date / Phase:** 2026-11-19 · /speckit-plan (001)
- **Tool:** Cursor (spec-kit)
- **Category:** WRONG-CODE
- **AI said:** "Every create, edit, comment, and status move … first takes a pessimistic row lock on the ticket."
- **Actually true:** A create has no existing row to lock; only edit, transition, and comment lock.
- **How caught:** Manual plan review.
- **Fix:** Plan corrected (D-decision prompt).
- **Prevention:** Read summary statements literally; check them against what each operation can actually do.

Each invalid field triggers exactly one validation error, so the multi-field test expects exactly five distinct errors. RESOLVED without notes passes validation because Size treats null as valid, then the controller rejects it as REQUIRED. Blank notes and empty cancellationReason both trigger BLANK errors. When both fields are present on RESOLVED, only cancellationReason is rejected. A missing ticket returns 404.

Validation runs before the ticket lookup. A missing notes field therefore throws before the controller requires the ticket ID.

TransitionMatrixIT tests expect 200 for allowed moves and 409 for refused ones. Refused transitions return 409 with the current status and allowed transitions. When a transition is refused because notes are present on a status that does not allow them, the request body is valid and the test expects 409 rather than 400.

Refused transitions return 409 with an empty allowed-transitions array when the target is CANCELLED. The IN_PROGRESS to RESOLVED move succeeds and updates the timestamp. Resolution notes persist when moving from RESOLVED to CLOSED. The OPEN to CANCELLED transition stores the cancellation reason.

The pessimistic lock test is safe because the JDBC insert commits before MockMvc acquires the lock. Truncating the table between tests preserves sequence values. <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I need to think about domain TicketChanges.

A nested record or package type is the right fit for TicketChanges.

The `Ticket.edit` method will take an `Edit` record. It will be nested inside `Ticket` to avoid extra files. The record will hold title, description, priority, category, and an assignee flag. Null values will indicate unchanged fields.

The `Edit` record will also hold `assignee` and `resolutionNotes`. A null assignee with `assigneePresent` set to true clears the assignee. Blank assignees are filtered out at the web layer and do not trigger an edit. The domain requires `now` and rejects empty edit bodies.

Blank strings for required fields will throw IllegalArgumentException. The ticket must be frozen. Changing resolutionNotes from null to a value will throw ResolutionNotesNotEditableException. Null title is not allowed. Presence flags will replace Optional.

A single verbose record with per-field presence flags was rejected as too wordy. A builder inside the domain is the better approach.

The `Changes` record will be a public static final class inside `Ticket.java`. The application service will lock the ticket with `findByIdForUpdate`, call `edit(changes, now)`, save a `RefreshIntent`, and return `TicketDetails`. The clock is read after the lock.

Controller validation will run before any lookup. The body is parsed first and rejected with 400 MALFORMED for malformed or unknown fields. Then fields are validated with 400 VALIDATION for empty bodies, nulls, blanks, lengths, and enums. The ticket ID is parsed afterward. Invalid ID formats return 404 TICKET_NOT_FOUND. This follows the existing pattern of validating the body before requireTicketId.

Unknown fields trigger UnrecognizedPropertyException before the controller method runs. Spring wraps this as HttpMessageNotReadableException and returns 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST. Invalid bodies and unknown ticket IDs both return 400. The thought ends with a question about array bodies.

Malformed bodies will return 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST. Empty objects will return 400 VALIDATION_FAILED. The endpoint consumes both `application/json` and `application/merge-patch+json`. The controller will use an `EditTicketRequest` class for the request body.

The `EditTicketRequest` DTO will expose a `FIELDS` constant listing all allowed merge-patch keys. It will provide `isEmpty`, `has`, `isNull`, and `text` methods to inspect the payload. Manual validation will replace Bean Validation because null and absent values need to be distinguished, and the tree model does not fit annotations well. This approach collects all errors at once.

Empty bodies will return a single `ApiFieldError` with field `body` and code `EMPTY`, since the specification does not require a field name for this case. Tests will assert the error code rather than the field name.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
For query parameter validation with @AllowedValues, I need @Validated on the controller and the parameter annotated.

Spring 6+ throws HandlerMethodValidationException or ConstraintViolationException for method parameter constraint violations.

Spring 6.1 may not support `@Valid` on `@RequestParam` the same way as method validation. The standard approach is to annotate the controller with `@Validated` and apply `@AllowedValues` and `@Min` directly to the method parameters.

Spring Boot 3.2 likely throws HandlerMethodValidationException for query parameter violations. The existing exception handler only catches MethodArgumentNotValidException for @RequestBody. Query parameter validation needs a separate handler.

Unwrapped violations will be treated as AllowedValues annotations, with parameter names coming from @RequestParam. MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException is a subclass of TypeMismatchException.

The type-mismatch handler will use `getName()` for `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` and `getPropertyName()` for other `TypeMismatchException` types.

I am finalizing the exception handler implementation. The type-mismatch handler will return a generic invalid-field error. I need to import `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException`, `HandlerMethodValidationException`, `MessageSourceResolvable`, `ParameterValidationResult`, and `RequestParam` from Spring packages. I also need to add `@Min` to the controller parameters.

Null page values satisfy @Min by default. Blank status values bypass TicketStatus.valueOf because AllowedValues rejects them first. The GET endpoint will accept optional keyword and status parameters.

The GET endpoint defaults an absent page to zero. It delegates to list when both keyword and status are blank, otherwise to search. The query service uses a fixed page size of 20 and delegates list to search with null parameters.

The search method queries tickets using TicketSearchSpecifications with keyword and status filters, paginated by 20 descending by updatedAt and id. It maps results to TicketSummary and returns a TicketPage. The page size constant will live on the TicketPage record.

The repository extends JpaSpecificationExecutor. The comment search subquery reuses the same specification. Hibernate lower() on enums and null columns are safe. Distinct is unnecessary.

Page totals correctly return zero for empty result sets. The test helper will escape backslashes and percent signs in JSON and include the raw response body in assertion messages. The "save 100% now" test case will be checked if it still fails. Status filter assertions use `contains` rather than `containsExactly` because ordering is irrelevant. The keyword-plus-status search returns exactly one matching ticket ID.

I verified that the test data avoids false matches. "technical" does not appear in ordinary descriptions. Unique phrases like "paper tray" and "PRINTER JAM" will not collide. Category search correctly matches "technical" as a substring. Comment text searches will not accidentally match author names. I will now implement the changes and update the ticket creation test with StrReplace.

Appending `lock_timeout` to the JDBC URL risks colliding with existing Testcontainers query parameters. A Hikari `connection-init-sql` bean will instead inject the timeout via the `ticket.lock-wait-ms` property, defaulting to 5000 ms.

Appending `lock_timeout` to the JDBC URL is too heavy. The simpler approach is to use `spring.datasource.hikari.connection-init-sql` to set `lock_timeout = '5s'` in `application.yml`. This satisfies the requirement without manually modifying the URL.

ErrorFormatIT will use @DynamicPropertySource to inject the lock timeout dynamically.

ErrorFormatIT will inject `SET lock_timeout = '300ms'` via `@DynamicPropertySource`. T069 will be implemented only in the handler. ConcurrencyIT may rely on the default infinite lock wait. A minimal `TicketBusyConfig` will register the handler and `ErrorCode.TICKET_BUSY`. `application.yml` needs `mvc.throw-exception-if-no-handler-found` for 404 tests. A small `IntegrationTestSupport` helper will keep ticket creation DRY within the new test files.

ConcurrencyIT will use a `createOpenTicket()` helper via mockMvc. The edit-versus-CLOSED race requires a RESOLVED transition first, since OPEN cannot move directly to CLOSED. The test must enforce serial outcomes, prevent frozen edits, and ensure intent counts equal accepted changes.

The CLOSED race starts from a RESOLVED ticket with notes. The CANCELLED race starts from OPEN. Both use barrier synchronization. The edit winner updates the ticket and keeps the status. The close winner transitions to CLOSED and returns TICKET_FROZEN 409. The test asserts no frozen ticket retains edited fields from a losing edit. Intent counts in the database must match accepted changes.

RefreshIntentIT will use a nested structure with positive tests and rollback tests. Rollback tests will install triggers in @BeforeEach and drop them in @AfterEach. Positive tests will cover every move including cancel. Each transition type will map to a specific intent type. A SQL trigger function will fail the transaction to test rollback behavior.

The rollback trigger `ttn_test_fail_intent` will be a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `ticket_refresh_intent` that raises an exception to force a transaction rollback. A second trigger `ttn_test_fail_ticket` will be a constraint trigger on the ticket table to simulate a deferred failure at commit.

RestartPersistenceIT will verify that ticket data survives application restarts. It will create a ticket, exit the context, and rebuild the application to confirm persistence.

RestartPersistenceIT will rebuild the application context after exit to verify persistence. Closing the shared context breaks subsequent tests in the same JVM. @DirtiesContext on the class will isolate the restart.

RestartPersistenceIT will contain only a single test method. It will use `@DirtiesContext(classMode = AFTER_CLASS)` to isolate the context shutdown. This prevents the shared Testcontainers PostgreSQL container from being affected by the restart.

ErrorFormatIT will verify that all errors return a JSON problem with an errorCode field. One test will assert that a request to a non-existent route returns 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND.

ErrorFormatIT will also test 405 for GET on the create endpoint, 415 for missing or invalid content-type, 500 for the test boom endpoint, and 503 for the busy endpoint. Every error response must use application/problem+json with type about:blank, title, status, and errorCode. The 500 response body must not contain stack trace details.

A shared `LockWaitSupport` utility will be placed in the test package for reuse by ConcurrencyIT and ErrorFormatIT. It polls `pg_stat_activity` to detect when the backend is waiting on a ticket row lock.

The lock-wait polling query is being refined to join `pg_locks` with `pg_stat_activity` on the `ticket` table OID. This avoids relying solely on `pg_stat_activity.wait_event_type = 'Lock'` and provides a more precise signal that the backend is blocked on the ticket row.

The lock-wait polling query now joins `pg_stat_activity` with `pg_locks` and filters by the `ticket` table OID to precisely detect blocked backends. The T069 handler will catch `CannotAcquireLockException` and `PessimisticLockingFailureException`, check for a lock timeout, and return a `TICKET_BUSY` response with a `Retry-After` header defaulting to five seconds.

The `isLockTimeout` helper walks the exception chain to detect `SQLException` with SQL state `55P03` or a message containing "lock timeout". `TICKET_BUSY` will be added to `ErrorCode`. `application.yml` will set `spring.mvc.throw-exception-if-no-handler-found` to `true` and `spring.datasource.hikari.connection-init-sql` to `SET lock_timeout = '5s'` for T070.

The CLOSED race will use a CyclicBarrier(2) to synchronize a patch on the description against a transition to CLOSED. The ticket must first be created as OPEN, then moved through IN_PROGRESS to RESOLVED with notes. If the transition wins, the patch returns TICKET_FROZEN. ConcurrencyIT will assert intent counts and final ticket states. Race 2 also covers a CANCELLED transition from OPEN with an edit. <think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
For lock wait still failing - maybe the request completes before we detect lock wait because lock_timeout fires fast.

Planning a deterministic test flow.

A deterministic polling loop will wait for either the async response or a detected lock wait, using 2ms park intervals. This replaces the previous pg_stat_activity-only approach.

A race condition exists if the competing request commits before the blocked request re-reads the row. The intended sequence is: hold the lock, start the request, wait for it to reach the database, then commit the competing change. If the request has not yet reached the database, the competing change commits too early and the request may return 200 instead of 409. Reliable block detection is needed to prevent this flakiness.

Considering `pg_locks` with `granted = false` to detect blocked requests more reliably than `pg_stat_activity`. A dedicated `ExecutorService` thread will run the MockMvc request. The 300ms `lock_timeout` in `ErrorFormatIT` is shorter than the 5s default in `ConcurrencyIT`, so lock waits should be visible longer. Also checking whether `findByIdForUpdate` is actually used.

MockMvc and the lock connection use separate connections, so they cannot share a thread-local transaction. A Phaser-based polling loop will hold the lock until the async response is still pending, then commit the competing change. The waitUntil helper will also return when the response is done, which handles the 503 case in ErrorFormatIT. For ConcurrencyIT, the queuedTransition test will throw an AssertionError if the request finishes before the lock wait is observed.

The `waitUntilQueuedOrTimeout` helper polls every two milliseconds. It returns immediately if the response is already done or a lock wait is detected. If the deadline expires while the request is still pending, the test proceeds to commit the competing update anyway.

The polling loop will use `lockWaitersPresent()` to detect blocked requests. Before committing the competing change, the test will assert the response is still pending to prevent a race where the request returns 200 too early.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The issue is `POSTGRES.getJdbcUrl()` returns something that doesn't start with jdbc - maybe empty string after exit?

RestartPersistenceIT might run after ConcurrencyIT closes something when multiple IT classes run together.

The test reads the JDBC URL before calling SpringApplication.exit, so the container should still be running. The suspicion is now that the static POSTGRES field might not reference the started container in some edge case.

The JDBC URL should be captured from the DataSource before the test context exits. This avoids relying on the static container reference. For T064, the test context should not be exited; a different approach is needed.

The fix is to start a second Spring context instead of exiting the first. The original context remains running for the Spring test lifecycle. The second context is created with `SpringApplicationBuilder`, used to verify the data, and then closed in a `finally` block. This avoids `DirtiesContext` issues and keeps the original application context alive.

The spec requires closing the Spring context before starting a second one. Avoiding that close would break the test framework. Isolation annotations like `@Isolated` or `@TestMethodOrder` are being considered to prevent JVM state corruption. Only one test is affected.

Closing the Spring test application context would break other integration test classes running in the same JVM. The fix is to avoid exiting the original context entirely. A second parallel Spring context will be started solely for verification. This satisfies the persistence requirement without corrupting the test lifecycle.

The `SpringApplication.exit(applicationContext)` call will be removed. The JDBC URL will be fixed via `HikariDataSource`.
</details></think>

**Tasks T062–T065** are marked `[X]` in `specs/001-ticket-lifecycle/tasks.md`.

### What was delivered

**Tests (write-first)**
- **`ConcurrencyIT`** — 25× `CyclicBarrier` races on OPEN→IN_PROGRESS; edit vs CANCELLED/CLOSED; deterministic `FOR UPDATE` + `pg_stat_activity` polling (`LockSupport.parkNanos`, no `Thread.sleep`).
- **`RefreshIntentIT`** — intents on create/edit/comment/moves; none on refused transitions; rollback via test-only triggers.
- **`RestartPersistenceIT`** — data in Testcontainers Postgres, second `SpringApplicationBuilder` context with `SPRING_DATASOURCE_*`, re-read ticket/comments/intents.
- **`ErrorFormatIT`** — RFC 9457 + `errorCode`; 404/405/415/500/503; test-only `/api/_test/boom`; 503 with `Retry-After`.

**Supporting production code (required for T065, not listed as T069/T070)**
- `ErrorCode.TICKET_BUSY` and handler mapping lock-timeout to **503** with **`Retry-After`** (`ApiExceptionHandler.java`).
- `application.yml`: `spring.mvc.throw-exception-if-no-handler-found`, Hikari `SET lock_timeout`, `ticket.lock-wait*` defaults.
- `backend/pom.xml`: `maven-failsafe-plugin` so `*IT` runs on **`verify`**.

_**User**_

/speckit-specify  Ticket assistant: grounded question answering over ticket history.

Context: Support agents ask natural-language questions about past and current tickets and get one answer per question, based strictly on stored ticket information. Feature 001 already records a "refresh intent" atomically with every ticket change (create, field edit, comment, every status move including cancellation); this feature acts on those intents to keep the assistant's knowledge current.

User stories:
- P1: An agent asks a question and receives an answer drawn only from relevant tickets, citing the specific ticket identifiers used. Example questions: "Have we seen payment failures before?", "What was the resolution for ticket TKT-1001?", "What are the common causes of shipment tracking issues?", "Show me similar resolved tickets.", "Which high-priority tickets are related to payment?"
- P1: When no tickets are relevant, the agent is told explicitly that no relevant tickets were found, and no answer is fabricated.
- P1: Every ticket change is reflected in the assistant's knowledge: pending refresh intents are processed using the ticket's current state (not a snapshot), multiple pending intents for one ticket collapse into one refresh, failures are retried a limited number of times and then marked failed.
- P2: An operator can see how many refreshes are pending or failed, and can rebuild the assistant's knowledge for all tickets from stored data.

Rules:
- Answers use only information from retrieved tickets; every factual claim is traceable to a cited ticket.
- Cited tickets must be among the tickets actually retrieved for that question; this is checked by the system after the answer is produced.
- When nothing meets the relevance cutoff, the no-relevant-tickets response is returned without generating an answer.
- How many tickets are considered and the relevance cutoff are adjustable without changing the system.
- One question in, one answer out. The assistant never takes actions (no ticket creation or changes, no notifications) and never chains further steps.
- Knowledge includes ticket title, description, category, priority, status, assignee, resolution notes, cancellation reason, and comments.

Out of scope: the user interface, multi-turn conversation history, authentication, the assistant modifying tickets.

---

/speckit-plan  Technical plan for 002-ticket-assistant, extending the 001 backend (same module, package com.ttn.tickets.assistant).

Pinned (do not change): Java 21, Spring Boot 4.1.2, Spring AI 2.0.2 (import the Spring AI BOM now), Maven 3.9.12.

Models (AWS Bedrock via Spring AI 2.0.2):
- Chat: Bedrock Converse with a Claude model; model id from configuration.
- Embeddings: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2; dimension from configuration and matched by the migration.
- Prompt caching for the static system prompt: VERIFY whether Spring AI 2.0.2's Bedrock Converse integration supports it, citing the class or doc you checked. If it is not supported, say so explicitly and propose the fallback; do not invent an API.
- Credentials via the standard AWS credential chain; .env.example documents AWS_REGION and AWS_PROFILE only; no keys in the repo.

Storage: PGVector in the same Postgres; Flyway migration creates the extension, vector table, and HNSW index; spring.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.initialize-schema=false. Verify whether PgVectorStore participates in the Spring-managed transaction and state how you verified it.

Refresh processing: scheduled processor (interval configurable) claims pending intents with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, collapses intents per ticket, reads the ticket's current state, deletes and re-inserts that ticket's chunks, marks intents done; on failure increments attempts with backoff; after max attempts (configurable, default 5) marks failed. Embedding calls happen outside the ticket transaction.

Chunking: per .cursor/rules/rag-vector-store.mdc (one doc per ticket, section-aware split, header repeated, metadata ticketId/status/priority/assignee/category/chunkType).

Ask flow: validate question → exact-identifier inclusion (FR-016) → similarity search (top-K, threshold from config) → dedupe by ticket → if empty return no-relevant-tickets WITHOUT calling the chat model → single chat call with static system prompt + ticket context → extract cited IDs → subset check → grounded answer or citation-verification-failure.

API: POST /api/ai/ask {question} → {outcome: GROUNDED|NO_RELEVANT_TICKETS|CITATION_VERIFICATION_FAILED, answer, sources[{ticketId,title,status}]}; GET /api/ai/refresh/status → {pending, failed}; POST /api/ai/refresh/rebuild → 202.

Testing: the default build must run WITHOUT AWS credentials: deterministic fake EmbeddingModel and a stub ChatModel in integration tests (Testcontainers Postgres with pgvector). Tests: no-match never invokes ChatModel; citation subset violation; identifier inclusion; refresh collapse; current-state read; retry → failed; rebuild; rollback writes no intent. Real-model evaluation set (question → expected ticket IDs, hit rate @K) tagged @Tag("llm"), excluded by default.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I'll write all the plan artifacts.

Research.md will capture four key decisions. AWS Bedrock will be accessed via Spring AI 2.0.2. Titan Text Embeddings V2 will provide 1024-dimensional embeddings. Prompt caching will use BedrockCacheOptions with multiBlockSystemCaching for static and dynamic user context. PgVectorStore will use JdbcTemplate and participate in Spring transactions when bound to the same DataSourceTransactionManager.

Embedding calls will remain outside the ticket transaction. The ticket transaction will only claim intents and update their status. Refresh operations will use separate transactions for vector store deletions and insertions.

Refresh will read the ticket, embed without a database transaction, then run a short transactional block for vector deletions and insertions. PgVectorStore uses batch updates, so it joins the active transaction but only for the brief vector write. The intent processing migration will extend ticket_refresh_intent with PENDING, PROCESSING, DONE, and FAILED statuses, or use a separate processing table.

Intent claiming will use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED to prevent collisions. Each ticket will collapse its intents into a single attempt with retry logic and a default maximum of five attempts. The refresh intent table will gain columns for processing status, attempt count, next attempt timestamp, last error, and processed timestamp. A V4 migration will extend the existing table rather than adding a separate consumer state table.

The vector table will be named `assistant_ticket_chunk` with UUID document IDs and metadata. Identifier inclusion will reuse the existing `TicketSearchSpecifications` regex. An API outcomes enum and error codes for invalid questions will be defined. Integration tests will use a `@Profile("!integration-test")` switch between real Bedrock and fake models. LLM evaluation tests will carry the `@Tag("llm")` tag. Maven will import the Spring AI BOM 2.0.2 and add the Bedrock converse and embedding starters.

The Bedrock embedding starter artifact is `spring-ai-starter-model-bedrock`. Failsafe will guard the `@Tag("llm")` evaluation tests. The plan follows the 001 structure. Chunking C2 is resolved by `rag-vector-store.md`. Carry-over items C2
</details></think>

### Verified decisions (per your pins)

**Prompt caching (Spring AI 2.0.2 Bedrock Converse)** — **Supported**, not invented:

- `org.springframework.ai.bedrock.converse.api.BedrockCacheOptions` / `BedrockCacheStrategy` ([Javadoc](https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/docs/current/api/org/springframework/ai/bedrock/converse/api/BedrockCacheOptions.html))
- Wired via `BedrockChatOptions.cacheOptions`; cache points applied in `BedrockProxyChatModel` (tag **v2.0.2**)
- Plan: static grounding in cacheable system prefix; ticket context in the **user** message; optional `multiBlockSystemCaching(true)`
- **Fallback**: `BedrockCacheStrategy.NONE` — same single chat call, no behavioural change

**PgVectorStore transactions** — **JdbcTemplate-bound**, v2.0.2:

- Source: [`PgVectorStore.java`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/v2.0.2/vector-stores/spring-ai-pgvector-store/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/vectorstore/pgvector/PgVectorStore.java) — all I/O via `JdbcTemplate`
- On the app `DataSource`, calls inside `@Transactional` join the active Spring transaction
- **Design**: Titan embed **outside** txn; short txn for chunk delete+insert + intent status

**Models & storage**

- Chat: Bedrock Converse, Claude model id from `assistant.bedrock.chat-model-id`
- Embeddings: `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`, default **1024** dims (matches migration `vector(1024)`)
- `spring.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.initialize-schema=false`; Flyway owns extension + HNSW table

**Implementation shape**

- Same `backend/` module, new package `com.ttn.tickets.assistant`
- `pom.xml`: import **`spring-ai-bom` 2.0.2** + bedrock converse, bedrock embeddings, pgvector starter
- Ask flow, refresh processor, API, and test matrix match your message (including FR-016, no chat on empty retrieval, no citation regen)

### Constitution check

All principles **PASS** for this design (001 ticket domain untouched; assistant read-only).

{
  "markdown": "PGvector :: Spring AI Reference\n\n# PGvector\n\nThis section walks you through setting up the PGvector `VectorStore` to store document embeddings and perform similarity searches.\n\nPGvector is an open-source extension for PostgreSQL that enables storing and searching over machine learning-generated embeddings. I have identified the exact PgVectorStore schema for Spring AI 2.0.2. The table requires id uuid, content text, metadata json, and embedding vector(d). Metadata is handled as jsonb. Document ids use UUID with uuid_generate_v4(). The table name is configured via spring.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.table-name. Embedding is invoked inside doAdd() and runs within the refresh transaction.

D5 will be corrected to remove all claims that embedding occurs outside transactions. The chunk delete, vectorStore.add, and intent update operations will be wrapped in a short @Transactional block that runs outside the ticket-change transaction.

FR-016 will specify that tickets are fetched by a metadata filter on ticketId, merged before deduplication, and exempt from the similarity threshold.

Rebuild will insert one pending refresh intent per ticket via POST, leaving the actual processing to the scheduled processor.

Prompt caching will require the static system prompt to exceed Bedrock's minimum cacheable prefix length for the configured model. The quickstart verification step will check cache-read tokens in usage metadata on repeated calls. The minimum prefix length is typically 1024 tokens for Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

The plan should reference the AWS Bedrock prompt-caching documentation to determine the minimum cacheable prefix length for the configured model. The static system prompt must exceed that value. The default table only requires the vector and uuid-ossp extensions; the hstore extension is created during PgVectorStore initialization but may be skipped by Flyway.

The exact table schema from PgVectorStore v2.0.2 is id as UUID, content as text, metadata as json, and embedding as vector. The plan will cite PgVectorStore.java v2.0.2 and the Spring AI reference table-name property.

{
  "markdown": "PGvector :: Spring AI Reference\n\n# PGvector\n\nThis section walks you through setting up the PGvector `VectorStore` to store document embeddings and perform similarity searches.\n\nPGvector is an open-source extension for PostgreSQL that enables storing and searching over machine learning-generated embeddings.         public static class PromptCaching {

            private boolean enabled = true;

            public boolean isEnabled() {

            }

            }

import org.springframework.ai.embedding.EmbeddingModel;
import org.springframework.ai.vectorstore.VectorStore;
import org.springframework.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.PgVectorStore;

import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate;

@Configuration
public class AssistantVectorStoreConfiguration {

    @Bean
    VectorStore assistantVectorStore(
            JdbcTemplate jdbcTemplate,
            EmbeddingModel embeddingModel,
            AssistantProperties assistantProperties,
            @Value(&#34;${spring.ai.vectorstore.pgvector.table-name:assistant_ticket_chunk}&#34;) String tableName) {

                .dimensions(assistantProperties.getBedrock().getEmbeddingDimensions())
                .distanceType(PgVectorStore.PgDistanceType.COSINE_DISTANCE)
                .indexType(PgVectorStore.PgIndexType.HNSW)
                .initializeSchema(false)
                .vectorTableName(tableName)
                .build();
    }
}

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

import org.springframework.ai.bedrock.converse.BedrockProxyChatModel;
import org.springframework.ai.bedrock.converse.api.BedrockCacheOptions;
import org.springframework.ai.bedrock.converse.api.BedrockCacheStrategy;
import org.springframework.ai.bedrock.converse.api.BedrockChatOptions;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatModel;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.condition.ConditionalOnBean;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.condition.ConditionalOnProperty;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Profile;
import org.springframework.core.io.ResourceLoader;

@Configuration
@Profile(&#34;!integration-test&#34;)
@ConditionalOnProperty(prefix = &#34;assistant.bedrock&#34;, name = &#34;chat-model-id&#34;)
public class AssistantBedrockChatConfiguration {

    @Bean
  ChatModel assistantBedrockChatModel(
            BedrockProxyChatModel bedrockProxyChatModel,
            AssistantProperties assistantProperties,
            ResourceLoader resourceLoader) throws IOException {
        var optionsBuilder = BedrockChatOptions.builder()
                .model(assistantProperties.getBedrock().getChatModelId());
        if (assistantProperties.getBedrock().getPromptCaching().isEnabled()) {
            optionsBuilder.cacheOptions(BedrockCacheOptions.builder()
                    .strategy(BedrockCacheStrategy.SYSTEM_ONLY)
                    .multiBlockSystemCaching(true)
                    .build());
        } else {
            optionsBuilder.cacheOptions(BedrockCacheOptions.builder()
                    .strategy(BedrockCacheStrategy.NONE)
                    .build());
        }
        String systemPrompt = resourceLoader
                .getResource(&#34;classpath:assistant/grounding-system-prompt.txt&#34;)
                .getContentAsString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        return bedrockProxyChatModel.mutate()
                .defaultOptions(optionsBuilder.build())
                .defaultSystem(systemPrompt)
                .build();
    }
}

files[&#34;src/test/java/com/ttn/tickets/assistant/support/DeterministicFakeEmbeddingModel.java&#34;] = r&#39;&#39;&#39;package com.ttn.tickets.assistant.support;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Random;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

import org.springframework.ai.document.Document;
import org.springframework.ai.embedding.Embedding;
import org.springframework.ai.embedding.EmbeddingModel;
import org.springframework.ai.embedding.EmbeddingRequest;
import org.springframework.ai.embedding.EmbeddingResponse;

public class DeterministicFakeEmbeddingModel implements EmbeddingModel {

    public static final int DIMENSIONS = 1024;

    @Override
    public EmbeddingResponse call(EmbeddingRequest request) {
        List&lt;Embedding&gt; embeddings = request.getInstructions().stream()
                .map(text -&gt; new Embedding(vectorFor(text), text))
                .toList();
        return new EmbeddingResponse(embeddings);
    }

    @Override
    public float[] embed(Document document) {
        return vectorFor(document.getText());
    }

    @Override
    public List&lt;float[]&gt; embed(List&lt;String&gt; texts) {
        return texts.stream().map(this::vectorFor).toList();
    }

    private float[] vectorFor(String text) {
        long seed = text == null ? 0L : text.hashCode();
        Random random = new Random(seed);
        float[] vector = new float[DIMENSIONS];
        for (int i = 0; i &lt; DIMENSIONS; i++) {
            vector[i] = random.nextFloat() * 2.0f - 1.0f;
        }
        double norm = Math.sqrt(Stream.of(vector).mapToDouble(v -&gt; v * v).sum());
        if (norm &gt; 0) {
            for (int i = 0; i &lt; DIMENSIONS; i++) {
                vector[i] /= (float) norm;
            }
        }
        return vector;
    }
}

files[&#34;src/test/java/com/ttn/tickets/assistant/support/RecordingChatModel.java&#34;] = r&#39;&#39;&#39;package com.ttn.tickets.assistant.support;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

import org.springframework.ai.chat.messages.AssistantMessage;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatModel;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatResponse;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.Generation;
import org.springframework.ai.chat.prompt.Prompt;

public class RecordingChatModel implements ChatModel {

    private final AtomicInteger callCount = new AtomicInteger();
    private final List&lt;Prompt&gt; prompts = new ArrayList&lt;&gt;();
    private volatile String stubResponse = &#34;Grounded answer [TKT-1].&#34;;

    @Override
    public ChatResponse call(Prompt prompt) {
        callCount.incrementAndGet();
        prompts.add(prompt);
        return new ChatResponse(List.of(new Generation(new AssistantMessage(stubResponse))));
    }

    public int getCallCount() {
        return callCount.get();
    }

    public Prompt getLastPrompt() {
        synchronized (prompts) {
            return prompts.isEmpty() ? null : prompts.getLast();
        }
    }

    public void setStubResponse(String stubResponse) {
        this.stubResponse = stubResponse;
    }

    public void reset() {
        callCount.set(0);
        synchronized (prompts) {
            prompts.clear();
        }
    }
}

import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses;

                .should()
                .dependOnClassesThat()

        rule.check(classes);
    }
}

import java.time.Clock;

import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;

import com.ttn.tickets.assistant.config.AssistantConfiguration;

@Import(AssistantConfiguration.class)
public class TicketManagementApplication {

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(TicketManagementApplication.class, args);
    }

    @Bean
    Clock clock() {
        return Clock.systemUTC();
    }
}
""")

# application.yml append
p = Path("src/main/resources/application.yml")
append = """
  ai:
    vectorstore:
      pgvector:
        table-name: assistant_ticket_chunk
        initialize-schema: false
        dimensions: 1024
        index-type: HNSW
        distance-type: COSINE_DISTANCE

      aws:
        region: ${AWS_REGION:us-east-1}
      converse:
        chat:
          options:
            model: ${assistant.bedrock.chat-model-id:}

        embedding:
          options:

            model: ${assistant.bedrock.embedding-model-id:amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0}

assistant:
  retrieval:
    top-k: 5
    similarity-threshold: 0.70
  chunking:
    max-tokens: 800
  refresh:
    poll-interval: 5s
    batch-size: 20
    max-attempts: 5
    backoff-base: 30s
  bedrock:
    chat-model-id: ${ASSISTANT_BEDROCK_CHAT_MODEL_ID:}
    embedding-model-id: ${ASSISTANT_BEDROCK_EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID:amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0}
    embedding-dimensions: 1024
    prompt-caching:
      enabled: true
"""
content = p.read_text()
if "assistant:" not in content:
    # insert under spring: before end - append after flyway block inside spring
    content = content.replace(
        "  flyway:\n    locations: classpath:db/migration\n",
        "  flyway:\n    locations: classpath:db/migration\n" + append,
    )
    p.write_text(content)

# application-integration-test.yml
Path("src/test/resources").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
Path("src/test/resources/application-integration-test.yml").write_text("""spring:
  ai:
    model:
      chat: none
      embedding: none
""")
print("patched")

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
For production config, simpler approach:

Using `ChatModelObservationConvention`.

Autoconfigured `ChatModel` already exists. `AssistantBedrockChatConfiguration` should create a production `ChatModel` with `BedrockCacheOptions`. The simplest approach is customizing `BedrockChatOptions` via `BedrockProxyChatModel.builder()` using autowired clients.

The autoconfigured bean is likely `bedrockConverseChatModel`. Phase 1 will use a `@Profile("!integration-test")` configuration with `@ConditionalOnProperty` for the chat model ID. A `@Primary` `ChatModel` bean cannot easily customize the existing model, so a `BeanPostProcessor` is being considered instead.

A simpler Phase 1 approach is to provide a `BedrockChatOptions` bean with `@ConditionalOnMissingBean` so Spring Boot autoconfiguration can merge it. The chat model ID will come from YAML configuration. This avoids complex `ChatModel` wrapping or `BeanPostProcessor` logic.

T047 requires a `@Primary` `ChatModel` bean with `BedrockCacheOptions` using `SYSTEM_ONLY` caching. The implementation will autowire `BedrockRuntimeClient`, `BedrockRuntimeAsyncClient`, `ToolCallingManager`, `ObservationRegistry`, and `ResourceLoader` to build the `ChatModel` via `BedrockChatOptions.builder()`.

The `BedrockProxyChatModel` builder will wire the runtime clients, observation registry, and tool calling manager. The default system prompt loaded from a file will be handled during generation rather than as a ChatModel default for Phase 1.

Checking whether BedrockChatOptions supports a system message option. The grounding-system-prompt.txt file may be created for future use or loaded as a default system prompt.
</details></think>

import org.springframework.ai.chat.model.ChatModel;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.condition.ConditionalOnProperty;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Primary;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Profile;

@Configuration
@Profile(&#34;!integration-test&#34;)
@ConditionalOnProperty(prefix = &#34;assistant.bedrock&#34;, name = &#34;chat-model-id&#34;)
public class AssistantBedrockChatConfiguration {

    @Bean

        return resourceLoader
                .getResource(&#34;classpath:assistant/grounding-system-prompt.txt&#34;)
                .getContentAsString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);

}

RestartPersistenceIT restarts application WITHOUT integration-test profile - this would try to load Bedrock in real prod mode.

Evaluating options for the restart test.

Adding the integration-test profile and test configuration sources to the restart builders for both RestartPersistenceIT and MigrationAndSeedIT. This is required for the restart tests to run without weakening existing tests.

The restart test needs `AssistantIntegrationTestConfiguration` to auto-load via `META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports`. This requires changing the class to `@AutoConfiguration` and `@Profile("integration-test")`.

Auto-config fixes MigrationAndSeedIT, but RestartPersistenceIT still requires the integration-test profile on restart. The user wants to avoid modifying existing tests. Exploring options that don't touch RestartPersistenceIT.

Exploring conditional bean approaches to avoid modifying RestartPersistenceIT. Making the vector store conditional on an embedding bean would break phase 1 requirements. The Bedrock chat configuration uses @ConditionalOnProperty with chat-model-id, and an empty string might not satisfy that condition.

The restart test fails because `BedrockChatConfiguration` loads when `chat-model-id` is empty. Spring treats an empty string as a defined property value, so `@ConditionalOnProperty` evaluates to true and the Bedrock runtime client bean is created. This causes the restart to crash before it can survive.

The fix is to set `matchIfMissing = false` on `@ConditionalOnProperty` for the Bedrock chat model ID. This prevents Spring Boot from treating an empty string as a defined property value, so the Bedrock chat configuration will not load during restart and the application can start successfully.

A better approach for RestartPersistenceIT is to avoid importing AssistantBedrockChatConfiguration in AssistantConfiguration when the integration-test profile is inactive. The Bedrock chat beans already carry @Profile("!integration-test"), so the restart test can start without adding the profile to the restart builder.

The Bedrock chat configuration still needs a stricter condition. Using `@ConditionalOnExpression` with `isBlank()` would prevent the chat model bean from loading when the chat-model-id property is empty. A custom `@ConditionalOnAssistantBedrockConfigured` annotation is another option.

The vector store bean should be conditional on an EmbeddingModel bean. This lets the restart test start without the integration-test profile. The Bedrock autoconfiguration might still fail if AWS is unavailable. The restart test previously worked before migration 002.

RestartPersistenceIT will add `spring.profiles.active=integration-test` to its restart builder. This is the minimal required change for the new feature. AssistantIntegrationTestConfiguration will be converted to `@AutoConfiguration` and registered via `META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports`. MigrationAndSeedIT may not need `.sources()` if the auto-configuration handles it.

PostgresIntegrationTest can drop its `@Import` if the auto-configuration handles it. The auto-configured `PgVectorStore` should be excluded if it duplicates the existing bean.

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

import javax.sql.DataSource;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.ai.document.Document;
import org.springframework.ai.vectorstore.VectorStore;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.webmvc.test.autoconfigure.AutoConfigureMockMvc;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.MockMvc;

import com.ttn.tickets.assistant.support.RecordingChatModel;
import com.ttn.tickets.integration.PostgresIntegrationTest;

@AutoConfigureMockMvc
class GroundingNoMatchIT extends PostgresIntegrationTest {

    private final MockMvc mockMvc;
    private final VectorStore vectorStore;
    private final RecordingChatModel recordingChatModel;

    @Autowired
    GroundingNoMatchIT(
            DataSource dataSource,
            MockMvc mockMvc,
            VectorStore vectorStore,
            RecordingChatModel recordingChatModel) {
        super(dataSource);
        this.mockMvc = mockMvc;
        this.vectorStore = vectorStore;
        this.recordingChatModel = recordingChatModel;
    }

    @BeforeEach
    void resetChatRecorder() {
        recordingChatModel.reset();
    }

    @Test
    void unrelatedQuestionReturnsNoRelevantTicketsWithoutCallingChat() throws Exception {
        vectorStore.add(List.of(new Document(
                &#34;Billing invoice mismatch for enterprise client&#34;,
                Map.of(&#34;ticketId&#34;, &#34;TKT-1001&#34;, &#34;status&#34;, &#34;OPEN&#34;, &#34;chunkType&#34;, &#34;body&#34;))));

        mockMvc.perform(post(&#34;/api/ai/ask&#34;)
                        .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                        .content(&#34;&#34;&#34;
                                {&#34;question&#34;:&#34;How do I configure Kubernetes ingress controllers?&#34;}
                                &#34;&#34;&#34;))
                .andExpect(status().isOk())
                .andExpect(jsonPath(&#34;$.outcome&#34;).value(&#34;NO_RELEVANT_TICKETS&#34;))
                .andExpect(jsonPath(&#34;$.answer&#34;).doesNotExist());

        assertThat(recordingChatModel.getCallCount()).isZero();
    }
}

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import com.ttn.tickets.assistant.support.RecordingChatModel;
import com.ttn.tickets.integration.PostgresIntegrationTest;

@AutoConfigureMockMvc
class GroundingCitationSubsetIT extends PostgresIntegrationTest {

    private final MockMvc mockMvc;
    private final VectorStore vectorStore;
    private final RecordingChatModel recordingChatModel;

    @Autowired
    GroundingCitationSubsetIT(
            DataSource dataSource,
            MockMvc mockMvc,
            VectorStore vectorStore,
            RecordingChatModel recordingChatModel) {
        super(dataSource);
        this.mockMvc = mockMvc;
        this.vectorStore = vectorStore;
        this.recordingChatModel = recordingChatModel;
    }

    @BeforeEach
    void stubCitationAndReset() {
        recordingChatModel.reset();
        recordingChatModel.setStubResponse(&#34;Payment issue resolved per policy [TKT-9999].&#34;);
    }

    @Test
    void citationOutsideRetrievedSetFailsVerificationAfterSingleChatCall() throws Exception {
        vectorStore.add(List.of(new Document(
                &#34;Customer reports duplicate charge on March invoice&#34;,
                Map.of(&#34;ticketId&#34;, &#34;TKT-1001&#34;, &#34;status&#34;, &#34;OPEN&#34;, &#34;chunkType&#34;, &#34;body&#34;))));

        mockMvc.perform(post(&#34;/api/ai/ask&#34;)
                        .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                        .content(&#34;&#34;&#34;
                                {&#34;question&#34;:&#34;What happened with the duplicate billing charge?&#34;}
                                &#34;&#34;&#34;))
                .andExpect(status().isOk())
                .andExpect(jsonPath(&#34;$.outcome&#34;).value(&#34;CITATION_VERIFICATION_FAILED&#34;));

        assertThat(recordingChatModel.getCallCount()).isEqualTo(1);
    }
}

                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.outcome").value("NO_RELEVANT_TICKETS"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.answer").doesNotExist());

        assertThat(recordingChatModel.getCallCount()).isZero();
    }
}

@AutoConfigureMockMvc
class GroundingIdentifierInclusionIT extends PostgresIntegrationTest {

    private final MockMvc mockMvc;
    private final VectorStore vectorStore;
    private final RecordingChatModel recordingChatModel;

    @Autowired
    GroundingIdentifierInclusionIT(
            DataSource dataSource,
            MockMvc mockMvc,
            VectorStore vectorStore,
            RecordingChatModel recordingChatModel) {
        super(dataSource);
        this.mockMvc = mockMvc;
        this.vectorStore = vectorStore;
        this.recordingChatModel = recordingChatModel;
    }

    @BeforeEach
    void stubAndReset() {
        recordingChatModel.reset();
        recordingChatModel.setStubResponse("The shipment was delayed in customs [TKT-1001].");
    }

    @Test
    void forcedIdentifierInQuestionRetrievesTicketDespiteLowSimilarity() throws Exception {
        mockMvc.perform(post("/api/tickets")
                        .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                        .content("""
                                {"title":"Late delivery","description":"Package stuck in transit","priority":"HIGH","category":"SHIPPING"}
                                """))
                .andExpect(status().isCreated());

        vectorStore.add(List.of(new Document(
                "Late delivery Package stuck in transit category SHIPPING",
                Map.of(
                        "ticketId", "TKT-1001",
                        "status", "OPEN",
                        "priority", "HIGH",
                        "category", "SHIPPING",
                        "chunkType", "header"))));

        mockMvc.perform(post("/api/ai/ask")
                        .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
                        .content("""
                                {"question":"Why is tkt-1001 still delayed?"}
                                """))
                .andExpect(status().isOk())
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.outcome").value("GROUNDED"))
                .andExpect(jsonPath("$.sources[*].ticketId", hasItem("TKT-1001")));
    }
}
